item.title: Victorian election 2026 live results: Jess Wilson vows to ‘bring back hope’ to Victoria after historic victory over Labor
item.author: Stephanie Convery (now) and Josh Taylor (earlier)
item.content:encoded: Follow live updates and results tonight as Jess Wilson becomes state’s 51st premier, with Labor leader Ben Carroll projected to lose seatFederal politicians largely absent from state electionJust following on from the last post, it is notable that the prime minister, , did not do a press conference with the state premier, , during the campaign, and the federal Liberal leader, , did just one press conference with his state counterpart, , during the campaign.I give a shoutout to all those Labor party workers who are handing out how-to-votes, the candidates who are working their guts out, but they know that it’s going to be very, very tough.And we know that this election campaign has been dominated by really the sorts of issues that you get when a government’s been in for more than 10 years.Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: In South Sudan, I discovered more deaths as a result of Elon Musk’s U.S.A.I.D. cuts.

item.title: Two Médecins Sans Frontières staff killed by Israeli strike in Gaza, charity says
item.author: William Christou
item.content:encoded: MSF and head of WHO denounce attack on Gaza City clinic as Israel claims security guards were members of HamasIsraeli forces have bombed a clinic run by Médecins Sans Frontières in Gaza City, killing two of its staff members, the organisation has said.MSF said Israel directly struck the clinic, despite the fact that its location was known to the Israeli military and that it was well marked with MSF logos. The organisation denounced the attack and said that with the deaths of the two security guards on Saturday, Israel had killed 17 of its staff members during the war in Gaza.Continue reading...

item.title: Victorian election 2026: Labor suffers historic defeat as Coalition wins majority government
item.author: Benita Kolovos and Henry Belot
item.content:encoded: Jess Wilson to become state’s first popularly elected female premier as Ben Carroll loses seat in 2026 state election, and Greens and One Nation surge Victorian Labor has suffered a historic defeat, ending 12 years of government, with the Coalition winning majority government and the Greens securing a record number of seats.One Nation was on course to win more than 20% of the primary vote, but struggled to pick up lower house seats on a night when huge swings and three- or even four-party contests in many electorates made preference flows difficult to calculate.Continue reading...

item.title: Argentina fails to block UK-led oil drilling off Falkland Islands
item.author: Press Association
item.content:encoded: International tribunal rules there does not appear to be basis for believing Buenos Aires has jurisdiction on islandsArgentina’s attempt to block oil drilling off the Falkland Islands has been rejected by an international tribunal.Buenos Aires had called for the international tribunal for the law of the sea (ITLOS) to order a halt to the Sea Lion project, as part of its claim to sovereignty over the Falklands.Continue reading...

item.title: High-security prisoner used soap to escape despite being handcuffed and chained to officer
item.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
item.content:encoded: Exclusive: inmate from HMP Manchester now back in custody after 13 hours on the runA prisoner from one of England and Wales’s most dysfunctional high-security jails is believed to have used soap to help escape from officers while visiting a hospital for treatment.The 36-year-old detained at HMP Manchester managed to slip away despite being cuffed and chained to an officer, sources told the Guardian. He is believed to have lathered his metal cuff with liquid soap and slipped his hand out while being given privacy to use a bathroom.Continue reading...

item.title: US oligarchs enriched by ‘transactional’ Trump face fierce scrutiny in new Congress
item.author: Peter Stone in Washington
item.content:encoded: Democrats pledge aggressive investigations into Trump-allied billionaires and how president’s policies have boosted their bottom linesFor an elite circle of Donald Trump billionaire allies who lavished tensof millions of dollars on his campaign, vanity projects and crypto ventures, his second administration has boosted their bottom lines through lax oversight, tax breaks, federal contracts and other perks.But with Democrats winning control of Congress in the midterms, House and Senate investigations are being planned for 2027 into several Maga oligarchs in hi-tech and crypto industries, examining how their firms and the president benefited from his “transactional” governing style, according to Democratic lawmakers and scholars.Continue reading...

item.title: Deal with Epstein lawyer and accountant could block victims’ other claims, experts warn
item.author: Victoria Bekiempis in New York
item.content:encoded: Concern that settlement to resolve suit against pair may stymie legal claims that involve child sexual abuse materialAs the clock ticks toward final settlement for a sex-trafficking-related lawsuit against Jeffrey Epstein’s accountant and attorney, some experts are expressing concern that the agreement might stymie survivors’ search for justice in other litigation involving child sexual abuse images.The suit involves Darren Indyke and Richard D Kahn, who for decades worked as Epstein’s personal lawyer and accountant respectively. Both men also serve as executors of Epstein’s estate. Indyke and Kahn have insisted they knew nothing about Epstein’s crimes and have rejected allegations of wrongdoing.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Please can I have one more picture’: the US airmen accused of child sexual abuse in UK who avoided British trial
item.author: Rob Evans, Harry Davies, Louisa Loveluck and Emine Sinmaz
item.content:encoded: Guardian investigation reveals US military personnel, including ‘multi-child molester’, convicted in courts martial When Jacob Ozbirn, an American airman, drove to a country lane near a Derbyshire hotel one summer’s evening, he was expecting to meet a 12-year-old girl he had been grooming for sex.In the previous days, he had sent explicit messages to her and two other girls, encouraging them to send him naked photos, despite having been told by all three that they were aged 12 or 13.Continue reading...

item.title: My Six Months With Saddam Hussein
item.author: George Piro
item.content:encoded: As the Iraqi dictator’s chief F.B.I. interrogator, I learned how much pre-Iraq war profilers got wrong about him.

item.title: Drones ‘swarmed’ US army base at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk in November
item.author: Harry Taylor
item.content:encoded: Personnel told to take cover after ‘suspected unauthorised activity’ of six drones that were repelled but not recoveredDrones reportedly swarmed a US army base in Suffolk earlier this month and were not recovered after being repelled.Personnel at RAF Lakenheath were told to take cover on 13 November after “suspected unauthorised drone activity”. The US air force confirmed the so-called Charlie alert at the time, the second-highest threat level, but released few details. Sirens could be heard at the base. Iran is suspected of being involved.Continue reading...

item.title: Spain to vote in election that could put far right in power for first time since Franco
item.author: Sam Jones in Madrid
item.content:encoded: Socialist PM Pedro Sánchez’s high-stakes gamble could end in defeat to a coalition including the far-right VoxSpaniards head to the polls on Sunday to vote in a high-stakes snap general election that could put a far-right party in government for the first time since the country’s return to democracy after the death of Gen FranciscoFranco in 1975.Although the next election was not due until summer next year, Spain’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, called the vote in October after three rightwing and far-right parties voted down the emergency legislation that his government had proposed to address the country’s housing crisis.Continue reading...

item.title: DWP cyber incident ‘probably an attack’, says former UK chief technology officer
item.author: Kevin Rawlinson
item.content:encoded: Government took down pensions and benefits portal on Thursday but said regular payments will not be affectedA serious cyber incident that forced ministers to take down online benefits and pension services was “probably an attack”, the UK’s former chief technology officer has said.The Department for Work and Pensions took down several systems that appeared to still be offline on Saturday morning. David Knott, who led government technology until December 2025, said much infrastructure was outdated, and underinvestment in defence and increasing sophistication of attacks meant it was only getting more vulnerable.Continue reading...

item.author: Norimitsu Onishi and Renaud Philippe
item.content:encoded: Canada relies on Inuit and First Nations Rangers’ traditional knowledge of the land to protect its most inhospitable corners. But that knowledge is disappearing.

item.title: Woman ‘traumatised’ by Sainsbury’s shoplifting ban after staff facial recognition error
item.author: Jessica Murray and Rosie Peters-McDonald
item.content:encoded: Monia Indge, 58, who has terminal cancer, escorted from supermarket after staff using FaceWatch technology misidentified herA woman with terminal cancer has been left “traumatised and violated” after being falsely accused of shoplifting and banned from Sainsbury’s by staff using facial recognition technology.Monia Indge, 58, was shopping with her husband in the Walters Yard branch of Sainsbury’s in Bromley on 7 November when she was suddenly told to leave by a member of staff who told her she was “banned for life” from the store.Continue reading...

item.title: Freed From a Notorious Syrian Prison, but Still Trapped by Its Terror
item.author: Raja Abdulrahim
item.content:encoded: Ahmed al-Shalh expected to perish in Sednaya prison. Abruptly released after a decade, he reveled in marriage and fatherhood but struggled to shake his ghosts.

item.title: Palestinian tells of ‘devastating’ struggle after being made redundant by EU in Gaza
item.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
item.content:encoded: Mohammad Baraka unable to access redundancy pay for almost 20 years’ service as family’s situation becomes ‘increasingly desperate’A Palestinian man who worked for the EU in Gaza has told of a “devastating” struggle to survive after he was made redundant by bosses in Brussels.He was let go last year after being evacuated to Egypt but his redundancy payment was made to an account to which he has no access. “My family’s situation has become increasingly desperate,” said Mohammad Baraka, a former staffer at the EU border assistance mission (EUBam).Continue reading...

item.title: La succession: France’s wealthiest family said to be battling over who will take over LVMH
item.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
item.content:encoded: Bernard Arnault’s children – described as ‘modern-day French royals’ – are subject of rivalry rumours over who will succeed himThey are France’s richest family, leading the world’s biggest luxury goods empire, dressed in matching Dior suits – a clan so powerful they have been described as modern-day French royals.But in recent months, the family dynasty of Bernard Arnault, 77, the billionaire head of the LVMH group whose brands range from Louis Vuitton handbags to Tiffany jewellery, has become the subject of speculation about internal rivalry over which of his children could take over the company.Continue reading...

item.title: Yuri and I used to play football together. Then I spotted his name among Russia’s war dead
item.author: Pjotr Sauer
item.content:encoded: I had no idea he had gone to fight in Ukraine and without hacked data I would probably never have learned of his deathOne evening, after weeks spent counting Russia’s war dead, I began looking for names I might recognise.My colleagues and I had been working our way through more than 11m death certificates leaked from Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, and identifying nearly half a million Russian soldiers who had died in the war in Ukraine.Continue reading...

item.title: Australia’s east coast deluged by storms as roads flood and damaging winds forecast for NSW and Victoria
item.author: Australian Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Severe weather and flood watch warnings are in place as a storm band moves from central Queensland through NSW to Victoria and Tasmania The final weekend of Australia’s wettest spring on record for an El Niño year is delivering a deluge of storms and heavy rain.Severe weather and flood watch warnings were in place across the eastern states as a weather band moves from central Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria and Tasmania.Continue reading...

item.title: Some Americans canceled or postponed Thanksgiving dinners amid power outages and storms.
item.author: Katie Benner, Mack Liederman and Emma Schartz
item.content:encoded: Some Americans canceled or postponed Thanksgiving dinners amid power outages and storms. They were rescheduled to Friday, Saturday and beyond.

item.title: Purse found of woman, 24, swept from California beach three weeks ago
item.author: Keely Aouga
item.content:encoded: Se Nah Park was overwhelmed by a wave at the notorious Panther BeachThe purse of a 24-year-old who was swept into the ocean at a notorious California beach three weeks ago was found on Wednesday, as the west coast saw record high king tides.The Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office confirmed that Se Nah Park’s purse was found by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach, south of Panther Beach, where she was swept away into the ocean on 8 November.Continue reading...

item.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for allegedly stealing trade secrets
item.author: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lawsuit also alleging pressure on hardware suppliers comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching employeesOpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the company of ⁠stealing its trade secrets ​and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices.The suit, filed in northern California federal court, comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.Continue reading...

item.title: Thousands still without power after storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel
item.author: Edward Helmore and agencies
item.content:encoded: Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to VirginiaSkies cleared along the US eastern seaboard on Friday, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers whose Thanksgiving plans were disrupted by heavy rains and high winds that swept over the region a day earlier.The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament
item.author: Keely Aouga
item.content:encoded: Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, a sign of the strained relations between the neighboring countries.Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it. The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”.Continue reading...

item.title: Police suspect criminals robbed fans at Manchester gig disrupted by ‘unknown substance’
item.author: Caroline Davies
item.content:encoded: Police are working with agencies across Europe after similar incidents occurred at two other Don Toliver concertsGreater Manchester police said they were working to identify the suspects and the substance involved during the incident at the Co-op Live Arena on Sunday evening.Continue reading...

item.title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
item.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
item.content:encoded: Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rightsCanada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning, the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.Continue reading...

item.title: Jess Wilson’s plan for Melbourne sewage plants risks water and wetlands without bringing debt down, experts say
item.author: Josh Taylor
item.content:encoded: Academic says Victorian Liberal proposal to privatise treatment plants and generate profit with no compromise of services ‘a total furphy’Experts have warned the Victorian Liberals’ plan to lease Melbourne’s sewage treatment plants is a “smoke and mirrors” way to pay off debt that risks compromising the state’s water resources and crucial wetlands for nearly a century.Continue reading...

item.title: Labor faces prospect of electoral wipeout in Victoria as voters turn to Liberals and One Nation
item.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
item.content:encoded: Former ALP strategist says Ben Carroll government at risk of losing more than 30 seats in Saturday’s election, to fall behind Pauline Hanson’s partyThe Victorian Labor government is facing an electoral wipeout after 12 years in office as the state heads to the polls on Saturday.Polling during the campaign has consistently pointed to a Coalition victory. The final Newspoll, released on Thursday, showed the Coalition 15 points ahead on a two-party-preferred basis.Continue reading...

item.title: Momentous decision looms after judges call for Netanyahu charges to be dropped
item.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
item.content:encoded: Dropping of corruption charges against Israeli PM after unusual intervention could set damaging precedentThe Israeli judges presiding over Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial have called on prosecutors to end proceedings, a highly unusual intervention that leaves the attorney general facing a momentous political decision.Continue reading...

item.title: Mad about mara: the DIY dance movement helping young Nigerians escape the daily grind
item.author: Eromo Egbejule in Lagos
item.content:encoded: What started as one artist’s response to being cut out of a music video has exploded, becoming a driving force in Nigeria’s cultural landscapeAs a student in the central Nigerian city of Ilorin, Lawal Habeeb Kola loved staying in his hostel room to produce beats rather than returning to his family house in Lagos, the more frenetic city of his birth.In 2022, one of his beats became popular on TikTok, and a version featuring ad-libbed vocals from a hypeman sent it viral. He was invited to the music video shoot in Lagos and thought his big break had finally come, but when the video was released, he was absent.Continue reading...

item.title: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern
item.author: Eva Corlett in Wellington
item.content:encoded: Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another electionThe final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.Continue reading...

item.title: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections
item.author: Amy Hawkins and Yu-chen Li in Taipei
item.content:encoded: Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling partyTaiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years, are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.Continue reading...

item.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says
item.author: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
item.content:encoded: Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza CityIsraeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter.On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”Continue reading...

item.title: Oxford museum displays seized belongings of Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu for first time
item.author: David Batty
item.content:encoded: Notebooks, clothes and ritual objects taken by British forces in India in the 1930s go on show at Pitt Rivers MuseumIn 1932, British forces in north-east India imprisoned a 17-year-old girl called Gaidinliu for leading an uprising against colonial rule. While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions.They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets.Continue reading...

item.title: Politician hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
item.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
item.content:encoded: Six helipads built and feast prepared by 500 cooks for wedding hosted by Anant Singh, a politician charged with murderIt takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024. Estimates of the cost for the months-long celebration ran to at least $600m, with world leaders and celebrities among those on the guest list.Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.Continue reading...

‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record
item.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
item.content:encoded: The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association.Continue reading...

item.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
item.author: Rebecca Bailey and agencies
item.content:encoded: Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.Continue reading...

item.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
item.author: Emma Graham-Harrison and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
item.content:encoded: Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decadeIsrael has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
item.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
item.content:encoded: Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far eastThe wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.Continue reading...

item.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charredA crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.Continue reading...

item.title: UN sacked Palestinian staff on back of unproven Israeli allegations, tribunal rules
item.author: Julian Borger Senior international correspondent
item.content:encoded: Judgment casts doubt on evidence linking aid workers to Hamas and says humanitarian efforts in Gaza were damagedA UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.The judgment, seen by the Guardian, raises fresh questions about the decision by the UN Relief and Works Agency (Unrwa), the main humanitarian organisation working in Gaza, to sack members of staff. It was taken on the basis of Israeli allegations of involvement in the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.Continue reading...

item.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
item.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
item.content:encoded: Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre endsColombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as ahostage-taker was killed.Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.Continue reading...

item.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
item.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
item.content:encoded: Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have childrenThe controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.Continue reading...

item.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
item.author: Rebecca Bailey and agencies
item.content:encoded: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong stationChina has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.Continue reading...

item.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
item.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
item.content:encoded: Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national parkA Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.Continue reading...
